channel.title: Molecular & Cell Biology Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Nature Cell Biology, Nature Communications, Molecular Cell, Nature Structural & Molecular Biology, Science Advances, and The EMBO Journal.

item.title: Nature Communications: Monolithic 6-Axis Force/Torque Sensing by a Single Ultrathin Piezoceramic Shell
item.description: A monolithic 6-axis force/torque sensor utilizing a single ultrathin piezoceramic shell achieves high sensitivity and decoupling accuracy through intrinsic mechanical deformation. This design simplifies calibration and enhances integration into robotics and wearable devices.

item.title: Nature Communications: In-tandem electrocatalysis via Ni single atoms and reconstructed Cu single clusters for CO 2 -to-acetone reduction
item.description: Electrochemical CO 2 conversion to multi-carbon products is hindered by inefficient C–C coupling. Here, the authors report a nickel single atom/copper single cluster catalyst that achieves high acetone selectivity through tandem catalysis, confinement, and in situ-formed Cu 0 /Cu + sites.

item.title: Nature Communications: Reversible layered/non-layered phase transition in a topological semimetal
item.description: Phase transitions in layered materials can differ significantly from those in non-layered materials. Here, the authors demonstrate a reversible phase transition between layered and non-layered phases in the semimetal PtBi 2 , resulting in a layered/non-layered topological phase transition.

item.title: Nature Communications: On the nature of chemical short-range order evolution
item.description: In situ synchrotron dilatometry and atomistic simulations indicate that changes between chemical short-range order states (evolving local chemical distributions) are governed by a kinetic arrest phenomenon rather than a thermodynamic transition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mechanistic studies of the human NIPA2 transporter
item.description: Here the authors show that the human NIPA2 transporter – a highly conserved member of the Drug Drug/Metabolite Transporter family linked to neurological disease – functions as a nucleotide transporter and may use a distinct translocation mechanism.

item.title: Nature Communications: Enhancing Phonon Group Velocities and Interfacial Heat Conduction for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
item.description: Low thermal conductivity of hole-transport layers in perovskite solar cells causes heat buildup, energy loss, and reduced stability. Wu et al. introduce a copper bismuth oxide composite layer to improve heat flow, achieving higher efficiency and long-term device stability.

item.title: Nature Communications: Dynamic catalytic interface driven three-step synergistic mechanism for boosting ammonia and hydroxylamine synthesis
item.description: The microscopic mechanism of nitrate-to-ammonia electrosynthesis remains ambiguous given the complex dynamic catalytic interface. Here, the authors report a three-step synergistic mechanism that enhances the interaction among interfacial H 2 O transport, *H generation, and *NOx hydrogenation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Widespread tropical cyclone activity during the Late Paleozoic Ice Age
item.description: A combination of high-resolution (~25-km) simulations and storm deposits point to widespread tropical cyclone activity during the Late Paleozoic Ice Age and a poleward shift in response to CO 2 -induced glacial-interglacial transitions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Root-inspired hierarchical hydrogel-electrode interface enables ultrasensitive sensing
item.description: Hydrogels are promising for physiological signal monitoring, though they are challenging to optimize surface engineering without compromising signal stability. Here the authors report a root-inspired hydrogel electrode for low pressure sensing.

item.title: Nature Communications: Towards an enzyme cascade synthesis of the bulk chemical acrylic acid
item.description: Acrylic acid is a bulk chemical produced via fossil-based processes. Here the authors repurpose a thiamine diphosphate (ThDP)-dependent enzyme to catalyze \({{{\rm{H}}}}_{2}{{{\rm{PO}}}}_{4}^{-}\) elimination from dihydroxyacetone phosphate for acrylic acid synthesis and establish a methanol-to-acrylic acid pathway.

item.title: Nature Communications: Symmetry-driven gating of TRPM8 by PIP 2 and menthol
item.description: TRPM8 ion channels are central to cold and menthol sensation. Here, the authors present various cryo-EM structures of TRPM8, including a two-fold symmetric intermediate and a menthol-bound sensitized conformation, revealing how PIP 2 and cooling agonists allosterically activate TRPM8.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-dose administration of therapeutic divalent siRNA targeting MECP2 prevents lethality in an MECP2 duplication mouse model
item.description: Here authors designed a durable, fully chemically modified therapeutic siRNA targeting MECP2 for MECP2 Duplication Syndrome. In a severe mouse model, a single dose of lead siRNA modified behavioral signs and rescued lethality for up to a year.

item.title: Nature Communications: An immune-poised state of human bronchial epithelial cells mediates defense against RSV in adults
item.description: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) often causes severe illness in young children but not in adults. In this study, the authors identify an immune memory response at the RIG-I-STAT3 axis in adult bronchial epithelia that facilitates age-related protection against severe RSV disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Transcranial focused ultrasound modulates spiking, LFP, and BOLD activity in the primate thalamus
item.description: Here, the authors show that low-intensity focused ultrasound induces BOLD activation and modulates low frequency local field potentials and spiking in the thalamic VPL nucleus and through remote sonication of the insular cortex. FUS responses show slower latencies than vibrotactile stimulation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fluorofenidone ameliorates pressure overload-induced heart failure by stabilizing SERCA2a in male mice
item.description: Reduced expression and activity of cardiac sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2 + -ATPase 2a (SERCA2a) are regarded as hallmarks of heart failure. Here, the authors show how the SERCA2a-targeted small-molecule agent fluorofenidone protects against pressure overload-induced heart failure.

item.title: Nature Communications: Small-scale photonic Kolmogorov-Arnold networks using standard telecom nonlinear modules
item.description: Photonic neural networks usually rely on power-hungry optical-electronic conversions for nonlinearity. Here, authors build a Kolmogorov-Arnold network whose every edge is one telecom module-an interferometer, amplifier and attenuators-trained end-to-end with a differentiable physics model.

item.title: Nature Communications: Solar and thermal dual-band electrochromic windows for energy-efficient buildings
item.description: Traditional electrochromic windows cannot regulate long wave infrared thermal radiation. Here, the authors report a solar and thermal dual-band electrochromic window that independently modulates solar transmission and thermal emissivity, enabling year-round building energy savings.

item.title: Nature Communications: Integrated device for optoacoustically-guided ultrasound surgery
item.description: High-intensity focused ultrasound can treat disease by heating tissue, but monitoring the treatment is difficult. Here, the authors use 3D optoacoustic imaging integrated with ultrasound therapy to safely guide the treatment in animal models, paving the way for safer, more precise brain therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: High-throughput antigen discovery using Functional Genomic Vaccinology (FGV) identifies protective Streptococcus pneumoniae vaccine candidates
item.description: To aid vaccine development against Streptococcus pneumoniae , the authors report a high-throughput antigen discovery platform integrating genome-wide antigen prediction, proteome-scale screening, and experimental immunogenicity validation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Host-directed treatments for tuberculous meningitis utilizing a multi-platform approach across mouse and human models
item.description: Here, the authors investigate a diverse panel of 12 immunomodulatory drugs as host directed treatments (HDTs) for tuberculous (TB) meningitis in a preclinical model, a human brain organoid model and cells collected from patients with TB meningitis.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structural and functional basis of antinociceptive action of χ-conotoxin AoIA at the noradrenaline transporter
item.description: Belleza, Zhang and colleagues showed that the χ-conotoxin χ-AoIA, a venom-derived peptide, reduces pain in mice by blocking the norepinephrine transporter more effectively than other similar peptides.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Mitochondrial-derived vesicles drive budding-type fission of damaged lysosomes
item.description: Luo et al. describe a budding type of lysosome fission linked to delivery of MFF from mitochondrial-derived vesicles to lysosomes. MFF recruits DRP1 for membrane scission. This axis restores lysosome function during hypoxia–reoxygenation stress.

item.title: Molecular Cell: RNA exonuclease REXO4 resolves m6A-marked R-loops and suppresses anti-tumor immunity
item.description: Zhang et al. reveal that the RNA exonuclease REXO4, guided by m6A modification, sustains R-loop homeostasis and genome integrity. Genetic loss or pharmacological inhibition of REXO4 triggers immunogenic interferon signaling and tumor immune infiltration, creating a synergistic vulnerability to PD-1 checkpoint inhibition in squamous cell carcinoma.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Structures of dynamic interactors at native proteasomes by PhIX-MS and cryo-electron microscopy
item.description: Lee et al. developed PhIX-MS, a UV-activated crosslinking structural proteomics workflow that traps transient interactions in cells to provide residue-to-residue distance information. These data are integrated with AlphaFold and/or cryo-EM to solve structures of the 26S or 19S proteasome bound to transient interactors, notably UBE3C, PSMD5, and TXNL1.

Molecular Cell: Thermo-sensing mechanisms of splicing control by nuclear stress bodies
item.description: Ueno et al. show that the phosphorylation of CLK1 functions as a molecular switch controlling its temperature-dependent localization to nuclear stress bodies. This regulation is mediated by a multilayered thermosensing mechanism involving PPP1R2, an intrinsically disordered thermosensor regulating PP1-mediated dephosphorylation during stress, and RIOK2-dependent rephosphorylation during recovery, coordinating temperature-dependent pre-mRNA splicing.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Conformational plasticity of human acid-sensing ion channel 1a
item.description: Using cryo-electron microscopy, Cahill, Hartfield et al. identified six structural states of human acid-sensing ion channel 1a, revealing how acidic conditions and peptide toxins regulate channel activation and desensitization through conformational flexibility.

Molecular Cell: Granular component sub-phases direct ribosome biogenesis in the nucleolus
item.description: Dogra et al. use super-resolution microscopy to uncover the molecular origins of spatial heterogeneity in the nucleolar granular component (GC). They show that differential interactions of nucleolar proteins, including ribosomal assembly factors, with ribosomal RNA generate distinct GC sub-phases that enable an assembly-line-like mechanism governing ribosome biogenesis.

item.title: Molecular Cell: SMD2 reads pseudouridines to regulate mRNA splicing and promote tumorigenesis
item.description: Meng et al. identify SMD2 as a reader of pseudouridine (ψ) in mRNA. SMD2 colocalizes with ψ near exon-intron junctions and preferentially recognizes ψ-modified transcripts to regulate mRNA alternative splicing. SNRPD2 is highly expressed across multiple cancers, thus highlighting the therapeutic potential of targeting the ψ-SMD2 axis.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: ESCRT-III assembles around mis-segregated DNA to protect genome stability
item.description: The authors show that persistent ultrafine DNA bridges become coated by membranes and the ESCRT-III proteins CHMP1B and IST1, which protect the genome within from damage.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: A conserved basic motif mediates membrane anchoring and TRAF2 recruitment across costimulatory TNFRs
The EMBO Journal: Metabolic buffering restricts phenotype switching in melanoma
Nature Cell Biology: Single-cell transcriptomics uncovers endothelial progenitor-like remodelling driving human coronary atherosclerosis progression
item.description: Yao, Li, Gai et al. profile normal coronary artery and early and advanced coronary atherosclerosis samples from humans using single-cell transcriptomics and identify a progenitor-like endothelial subtype with functional implications in disease progression

item.title: Molecular Cell: Large-scale quaternary structural transitions underlie gain of function of SPOP cancer mutations
item.description: Gain-of-function mechanisms of enzymes are generally poorly understood. Cuneo et al. reveal that the ubiquitin ligase component SPOP exists in an equilibrium between an active filament and an autoinhibited “double-donut” state. Activating mutations shift the equilibrium toward the active state, which results in aberrant substrate turnover and cancer pathogenesis.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: CST complex promotes second-strand synthesis in break-induced replication
item.description: Here Thakre, Wang and Liu and colleagues show that the Cdc13–Stn1–Ten1 complex helps cells to repair broken DNA by enabling synthesis of the second DNA strand during break-induced replication, a process important for genome stability and telomere maintenance in some cancers.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: CDK8 remodels the tumor microenvironment and promotes resistance to KRAS G12D inhibitors and daraxonrasib in PDAC
The EMBO Journal: Spalt-related is an inhibitor of mTORC1-mediated growth activated by the integrated stress response
Nature Cell Biology: Decoding stage-specific functions of PRC2 in early embryogenesis uncovers roles in preimplantation development and primordial germ cell fate
item.description: Zhou, Wang et al. dissect the role of PRC2 in early embryogenesis through inducible degradation of EED, a core PRC2 subunit, and report that PRC2 is required for proper maternal-to-zygotic transition and promotes epiblast specification.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Oncogenic EGFR rewires STING-TBK1 signalosomes to license DNA damage tolerance in NSCLC
The EMBO Journal: Mechanical constraints regulate embryonic stem cell mitosis in the developing brain
Molecular Cell: The UFSP2-ODR4 complex spatially confines and dynamically controls UFM1 deconjugation to safeguard neuronal proteostasis
item.description: Mao et al. demonstrate that reversible UFMylation is required to complete ER-associated ribosome quality control. The deUFMylation enzyme UFSP2 localizes to the ER via its interaction with the ER-resident protein ODR4 and functionally associates with the UFM1 E3 ligase complex to remove UFM1 from RPL26 on the 60S ribosomal subunit, thereby maintaining neuronal proteostasis.

item.title: Molecular Cell: A conserved mechanism of membrane fusion in nuclear pore complex assembly
item.description: Fischer et al. uncover a fundamental mechanism of membrane fusion during nuclear pore complex (NPC) assembly. Brl1 and Brr6 form ring-shaped, membrane-remodeling complexes that interact and bridge the nuclear envelope at NPC-assembly sites to mediate fusion. This pathway is conserved in humans via the metazoan fusogen CLCC1.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Cytoplasmic lattices store developmentally poised degradative and cytoskeletal complexes in mammalian eggs
item.description: Li et al. obtain high-resolution, native structures revealing that cytoplasmic lattices in mammalian eggs organize and store degradative and cytoskeletal complexes for early embryonic development.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Inhibition of lagging strand replication by G-rich telomeric DNA and the shelterin subunit POT1
The EMBO Journal: Alterations in chromatin organization promote totipotent-like features in a DPPA2/DUX-dependent manner
The EMBO Journal: Local autophagy impairment triggers brain-wide presynaptic remodeling and resilience
The EMBO Journal: Structure and receptor recognition of type-II feline infectious peritonitis virus spike glycoprotein
The EMBO Journal: PP2A phosphatase regulates Hippo signalling in dual manner
Nature Cell Biology: CD44 restricts EGFR mobility to polarize cytoskeletal signalling modules driving bleb-based migration
item.description: Jha et al. show that the transmembrane protein CD44 restricts EGFR mobility to maintain an EGFR–PI3K–Rac gradient during bleb-based cell migration.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Evolutionarily conserved short linear motifs drive actin filament binding
item.description: Paraschiakos, Yuan et al., using a computational pipeline, identify the short linear actin filament-binding motif (SFM) as an evolutionarily conserved actin filament-binding motif present in 103 human proteins.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Promoter reinforcement supports transcriptional resilience in drug-resistant cancer
item.description: Kameswaran et al. show that cancer cells can restore gene expression after TEAD inhibition by shifting control from enhancers to promoters, a process termed ‘promoter reinforcement’, enabling transcription despite disrupted promoter–enhancer communication.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: SenFlag gene signature identifies senescent cells in mouse and human tissues through a conserved core transcriptional program
The EMBO Journal: The TPR2 corepressor forms condensates with repressors to fine-tune growth and development in rice
The EMBO Journal: Mitochondrial calcium regulates lipid metabolism by modulating tethering of mitochondria to lipid droplets
The EMBO Journal: Essential nucleus-apical pole linkage maintains division fidelity during Plasmodium progeny formation
The EMBO Journal: Scalable phosphotyrosine enrichment with SH2 superbinder enables deep profiling of EGF responses
Molecular Cell: Spliceosomal proofreading factors safeguard 3′ splice-site fidelity and prevent proteotoxicity and inflammation
item.description: Li et al. uncover a previously unrecognized layer of splicing quality control in mammals. By preventing erroneous splice-site selection, the spliceosomal factors AQR, SYF1, and SYF3 protect protein homeostasis and suppress inflammatory pathology, highlighting the importance of splicing fidelity for tissue health.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Distinct ATRX functions cooperate with 9-1-1 and CST complexes to safeguard replication and telomere integrity
item.description: Segura-Bayona et al. uncover genetically separable ATRX functions that independently safeguard telomeres and genome replication, revealing how CST and 9-1-1 pathways suppress accumulation of toxic single-stranded DNA and preserve chromosome integrity.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Chromosome condensation mechanically primes the nucleus for mitosis
The EMBO Journal: NDR kinase SAX-1 controls dendrite branch-specific elimination during neuronal remodeling in C. elegans
Molecular Cell: A negative regulator of mitochondrial complex I assembly adapts respiration to cellular energy demand
item.description: Li et al. identify TMEM141 as a negative regulator of mitochondrial complex I assembly. Under high energy demand, the YME1L1 and AFG3L2 proteases degrade TMEM141, relieving its inhibition of the assembly factor TIMMDC1. This work reveals a mechanism that adapts complex I assembly to OXPHOS demands.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Substrate-induced assembly and functional mechanism of the membrane protein insertase SecYEG-YidC
The EMBO Journal: Assembly of the catalytic module and the rotor of human ATP synthase
The EMBO Journal: Conformational changes of the baseplate regulating tail contraction of Staphylococcus phage 812
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structural basis of asymmetric transcription through a composite nucleosome formed by a hexasome and an octasome
item.description: This study shows that RNA polymerase II traverses overlapping dinucleosomes (OLDNs) with direction-dependent efficiency. Cryo-EM structures further reveal how RNA polymerase II rearranges OLDNs, promoting directional transcription.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structurally defining neurokinin selectivity to improve NK2R agonists
item.description: The researchers used cryo-electron microscopy to map how synthetic agonists bind to the neurokinin 2 receptor to reveal the features that make them selective. These studies are a key step toward developing future obesity therapies that boost energy expenditure.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Cellular assembly and functional resilience of the mammalian RNA exosome
Nature Cell Biology: Cis and trans regulatory mechanisms of extrachromosomal DNA segregation
item.description: Xie et al. demonstrate that extrachromosomal DNA tethering to mitotic chromosomes is in part mediated by H3K27ac-marked chromatin, associated chromatin binders and transcription-associated cofactors.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Pairwise transmembrane domain insertion during multipass protein biogenesis
item.description: Multipass membrane proteins are mostly comprised of transmembrane domain (TMD) pairs, two TMDs linked by a short non-cytosolic loop. Smalinskaitė et al. show that TMD pairs are inserted as a unit by the Oxa1-family insertases EMC and GEL, not sequentially through the Sec61 protein translocation channel as was previously thought.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Catalytic activation of human Argonaute 2 requires RNA duplex deformation
item.description: Human Argonaute 2 requires distortion of the paired small interfering RNA (siRNA)–target RNA duplex, not just base pairing, to cleave targets. Structures show how RNA shape and key residues enable catalysis, explaining why some siRNAs are more effective.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structural basis of AtCas9 recognition of PAM mutants in underwound DNA topology
item.description: Cryo-EM structures of AtCas9 bound to underwound minicircle DNA reveal how DNA topology relaxes PAM recognition through topology-dependent interactions, providing a structural basis for near-PAMless CRISPR targeting.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: OMA1 protects from liver injury and tumorigenesis during aging by controlling hepatic immunogenicity
Nature Cell Biology: Mediator subunit MED4 enforces metastatic dormancy in breast cancer
item.description: Bae et al. identify MED4 as a regulator of tumour dormancy from a genome-wide CRISPR screen, and show that loss of MED4 alters the enhancer landscape and induces extracellular matrix remodelling to drive metastatic relapse in breast cancer.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structural basis of opioid receptor activation by PCP and ketamine
item.description: Jiang, Han and Fine and colleagues show that ketamine and phencyclidine can directly bind to and activate opioid receptors. Using structural and pharmacological approaches, they showed how these drugs interact with opioid receptors.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: mRAVE governs lysosomal catabolism through basal and mTORC1-regulated V-ATPase assembly
Nature Cell Biology: Lysosome-derived methylated arginine is a signalling metabolite controlling the lipidome
item.description: Nguyen et al. show that accumulation of dimethylarginine in lysosomes in disease models is associated with lipotoxicity and lipid droplet abundance.

item.title: Molecular Cell: FANCA-dependent FEN1 recruitment suppresses transcription-replication conflicts and PARPi sensitivity
item.description: Wang et al. uncover a non-canonical role for FANCA in safeguarding genome stability during DNA replication. FANCA recruits the flap endonuclease FEN1 to lagging strands to suppress transcription-replication conflicts, a function that becomes essential under oncogene-induced replication stress, rendering tumors vulnerable to PARP inhibition despite intact homologous recombination repair.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structural insights into OSTα/β-mediated transport of bile acids and steroid conjugates
item.description: OSTα/β regulates bile acid and steroid conjugate homeostasis. Sun, Tian, Low and colleagues reveal structures of the human OSTα/β transporter, elucidating mechanisms of tetramer assembly, substrate transport and drug inhibition.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structures of protein folding intermediates on the ribosome
item.description: Atomistic structural ensembles of protein folding intermediates on the ribosome are resolved by comprehensive 19 F nuclear magnetic resonance analyses integrated with molecular dynamics simulations, providing insights into cotranslational folding pathways.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: The oocyte-enriched metabolite serotonin alleviates cellular senescence and aging phenotypes in the mouse
Nature Cell Biology: Integrated stress response couples mitochondrial fitness with lineage reprogramming to drive cancer evolution
item.description: Diao, Zou et al. demonstrate that activation of the integrated stress response drives lineage dedifferentiation and tumour progression in lung adenocarcinoma, associated with aberrant mitochondrial function and metabolic fitness.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: ERO1a fosters glioblastoma aggressiveness and metabolic flexibility by regulating mitochondria-associated membrane dynamics
item.description: Bassot, Violy, Gorka, Cigalotto and colleagues identify ERO1a as a mitochondria-associated membrane protein that regulates calcium flux and mitochondria bioenergetics, which may be potentially targeted to inhibit glioblastoma growth in vivo.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: SPACA9 and MNMIP1 bridge the seam of spermatid manchette microtubules
Nature Cell Biology: TEAD1 condensates are transcriptionally inactive storage sites on the pericentromeric heterochromatin in cancer cells
item.description: Wang, Liang and colleagues show that the TEAD1 transcription factor can organize micrometre-sized nuclear biomolecular condensates independently of active transcription. TEAD1 condensates may act as depots for excess TEAD1.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: DRP1 and MID49 co-diffusion scans mitochondria for fission
item.description: Zollo et al. examine DRP1 behaviour at mitochondria: DRP1 diffuses along mitochondria in helical-like patterns influenced by MID49/MID51, scanning the organelle surface and stalling at preconstricted fission sites.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Mitochondria–ER contacts function as an iron supply hub
item.description: Oshio, Shiiba and colleagues show that HMOX2, which catalyses haem degradation, supplies haem-derived iron to mitochondria at ER–mitochondria contact sites in a process mediated by the mitochondrial ubiquitin ligase MITOL, also known as MARCH5/MARCHF5.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Long-range mutual activation establishes Rho and Rac polarity during cell migration
item.description: De Belly et al. show Rac induces membrane-tension-mediated mTORC2 activation to stimulate long-range Rho activation. Meanwhile, Rho-mediated contractility and blebbing at the opposite side of the cell may lead to PI3K-dependent Rac activation.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Semirandom DNA adducts regulate a filamentous defense-associated reverse transcriptase
item.description: Neville et al. show that DRT1 synthesizes semirandom DNA adducts to stabilize a filamentous state. C-terminal pseudoknots form along the axis of the filament. The pseudoknot conformation inhibits a nitrilase domain, preventing abortive infection.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Temperature and intrinsic Ca 2+ reshape TRPM4 pharmacology
item.description: Hu et al. show that physiological temperature and intrinsic Ca 2+ reprogram TRPM4 pharmacology, revealing hidden ligand activities missed under simplified assay conditions—even at structurally stable sites—and highlighting the need for environment-aware drug discovery.

Nature Cell Biology: Nucleophagy removes cytotoxic trapped PARP1
item.description: Hoslett et al. show that trapped PARP1 is cleared from the nucleus by nucleophagy involving the autophagy receptor TEX264 and p97. Inactivation of nucleophagy resensitizes acquired resistance of BRCA1-deficient cells to PARP inhibitors.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Diffusing caveolin-1 scaffolds regulate mechanosignalling
item.description: Mani, Tardif, Rossier et al. show that mechanical stress triggers caveolin-1 release from caveolae, enabling its diffusion in the plasma membrane and interaction with signalling effectors to regulate intracellular signalling.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Transcription-independent induction of rapid-onset senescence is integral to healing
item.description: Valdivieso, Rozmaric et al. show that wounding rapidly induces a senescent state in skin cells involving p21 protein induction, without the need for new transcription. These senescent cells are beneficial to early stages of healing.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: A transport-independent role for SLC25A12 in mitochondrial stress signalling
item.description: Jiang et al. show that SLC25A12 interacts with the mitochondrial protease OMA1, enabling activation of integrated stress response during mitochondrial damage. This role is independent of SLC25A12’s transport activity.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Distinct repair outcomes from single and convergent replication fork collapse
item.description: Here the authors show that collapse of single replication forks causes recombination, end fusions or degradation but does not restart DNA synthesis. In contrast, collapse of convergent forks completes DNA synthesis through error-prone double-strand break repair.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Membrane bridges and nanodomain partitioning govern membrane protein targeting to lipid droplets
item.description: Mizrak et al. use single-molecule tracking to dissect mechanisms of protein targeting to lipid droplets. They show that nanodomain-based confinement drives selective protein accumulation on lipid droplets.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Epigenetic programming by H3K23ac defines lineage fate of Meg3 + haematopoietic stem cells and drives immune ageing
item.description: Wei et al. show that Meg3 + haematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) expand upon ageing and present with an increase in H3K23ac levels observed already at middle age. Inhibiting H3K23ac ameliorates megakaryocyte/platelet and myeloid skewing in aged HSCs.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Dynamic regulation of H3K9 dimethylation drives mouse minor zygotic genome activation
item.description: Maeda et al. demonstrate that dynamic regulation of H3K9 dimethylation drives mouse minor zygotic genome activation (ZGA). Maternal H3K9 demethylases KDM3A/B remove H3K9me2 at ZGA gene loci during the two-cell stage, whereas H3K9 methyltransferases SETDB1 and G9a cooperatively repress these genes in mouse embryonic stem cells.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Soma-to-germline miRNA inheritance through yolk promotes stress resilience in progeny
item.description: In this study, the authors use the Caenorhabditis elegans model organism to show that maternal microRNAs are delivered from the intestine to embryos by the yolk, where they regulate gene expression and promote stress resilience in offspring.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Rap1-mediated steric hindrance protects telomeres from MRX sensing
item.description: The authors show that Rap1 protein coverage protects telomeres by physically blocking the Mre11–Rad50–Xrs2 NBS1 complex. Longer, denser Rap1 arrays better prevent DNA damage responses, providing a mechanism for how cells detect short telomeres and maintain genome stability
